summary: This continuation studies the polynomial dynamics of Markoff triples over finite fields. It imports the classical integer descent and surface conventions, proves the weight divisibility mechanism, develops the giant-orbit argument and its arithmetic estimates, and reaches prime and primitive squarefree approximation. Effective computation and nonabelian-level congruences have precise proof contracts; source corrections and unverified certificate inputs remain visible.

nodes.title: Extended Penner weights
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with 2≠0 and 3≠0. For x∈M*(K), if all coordinates are nonzero set w_i(x)=x_i/(3x_jx_k), where {i,j,k}={0,1,2}. Define by the indicated finite case distinction; prove independence of the order of j,k using commutativity.

nodes.title: Chen’s divisibility theorem
nodes.statement: For prime p>3, every finite subset S⊆M*(F_p) stable under all R_i satisfies p∣#S. In particular each V-orbit, each Γ-orbit and each graph component has size divisible by p. Together with the p=2 computation this holds for coefficient-three graphs precisely in the asserted range p≠3. It does not hold for their eight-point component at 3.
proofSteps: Restrict each R_i to S and apply involution balance separately to each coordinate weight.
Sum weight_sum over S: (#S:F_p)=(3/2)(#S:F_p). Rearrange using invertibility of 2 to deduce #S=0 in F_p.
Convert the cast equality into divisibility; use the separate p=2 enumeration.
acceptance: Use the invariant subset statement, which is stronger than a component-only target; retain the counterexample p=3.

On (b,c) it has matrix [[0,1],[-1,a]] and characteristic polynomial T²−aT+1. For a≠±2 define its order by the order of either root λ in F_{p²}ˣ; inversion leaves this order unchanged. At a=±2 use the actual unipotent matrix order, not the eigenvalue order.

Compute the matrix and characteristic polynomial; split the repeated-root cases before defining order.

nodes.title: Split and nonsplit conic sections
nodes.statement: For odd p and a≠0,±2, put κ=a²/(a²−4). If a²−4 is a nonzero square, choose λ∈F_pˣ with λ+λ⁻¹=a: t↦(a,t+κ/t,λt+κ/(λt)) parametrizes C₀(a) bijectively for t∈F_pˣ. In the nonsplit case use t∈F_{p²}ˣ with t^{p+1}=κ, and the same formula; this parametrizes C₀(a), with rotation t↦λt. Thus the slice sizes are p−1 and p+1 and all periods equal ord λ. At a=0 the nonzero conic has 2(p−1) points if −1 is a square and is empty otherwise. At ±2 it has 2p points if −1 is a square and is empty otherwise; the ±2 rotation periods are p and 2p respectively.
proofSteps: Solve the two eigenline coordinates, using a²−4≠0 and κ≠0.
For nonsplit λ^p=λ⁻¹; the coordinates lie in F_p exactly when t^p=κ/t.

nodes.statement: For every ε>0 there exist δ>0 and P such that for primes p>P, any Γ-orbit containing a coordinate of nondegenerate order L≥p^ε reaches the cage. nodes.title: The opening game
nodes.statement: There are c>0 and P such that for every prime p>P every Γ-orbit on X*(F_p) has at least c(log p)^(1/3) points. There is no finite Γ-orbit on X*(Qbar).
proofSteps: A finite characteristic-zero orbit forces all coordinate eigenvalues to be roots of unity; after a complex embedding their traces lie in [-2,2]. For u²+v²+w²=uvw the bound |uvw|≤(2/3)(u²+v²+w²) forces the origin.

For a purported small finite-field orbit, bound the three coordinate eigenvalue orders by its size, excluding the already large parabolic cycles. Put N equal to their lcm; p∤N. In Q(ζ_N), choose roots reducing to the given eigenvalues at a prime above p, and form the integral Markoff relation α.

The characteristic-zero argument makes α nonzero. RingOfIntegers.dvd_norm shows α divides its integral norm, so reduction at that prime forces p to divide the nonzero integer norm. Algebra.norm_eq_prod_embeddings bounds its absolute value by 20^{[Q(ζ_N):Q]}=20^{φ(N)}. Since N is at most the product of the three orders, obtain the logarithmic lower bound.
Treat orders 1,2 and trace zero separately; trace zero has eigenvalue order 4.
acceptance: The zero orbit must be excluded before the norm argument; a repeated-root parabolic cycle is already large.

nodes.title: Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak giant orbit
nodes.statement: For every real ε>0 there is Pε such that for every prime p>Pε the Γ-action on X*(F_p) has an orbit C(p) with #(X*(F_p)∖C(p))≤p^ε. For large p it is the unique orbit of size greater than half the total. This theorem first concerns Γ, not an arbitrary component of the Vieta graph.
proofSteps: Every coordinate with order at least p^η enters the cage orbit by the middle game.
Count traces with eigenvalue order below p^η by summing φ(d) over d∣p±1, d<p^η, with the subpower divisor bound.
Outside the cage orbit all coordinates have small order. Choose η sufficiently small relative to ε, then use the quadratic equation to bound the number of triples.
Use the point count to deduce uniqueness of the giant orbit.
acceptance: No proof step identifies a Γ-orbit with a Vieta component without the root adapter of MD.4.

nodes.title: Sparse exceptional primes
nodes.statement: Let E={p prime : Γ(p) is not transitive on X*(F_p)}, interpreting the empty coefficient-one locus at 3 by the stated vacuous transitivity convention. For every ε>0 there is Tε such that #{p∈E:p≤T}≤T^ε whenever T≥Tε.
proofSteps: Apply the arithmetic low-order curve theorem Q4 to the degree-four curves obtained by eliminating the fixed Markoff coordinate in eigenvalue variables.
Verify that these curves have no component contained in a translate of a subtorus; isolate the finitely many exceptional fixed coordinates.
Outside at most T^ε primes, all but boundedly many points on each relevant curve have a coordinate of order at least p^η.
The opening-game lower bound eventually exceeds the bounded exceptional set, so every orbit enters the cage.
acceptance: Generic low-order theorem is a supplier request, not a consequence of the existing Kummer Stepanov estimates.

nodes.title: The symmetric root orbit
nodes.statement: For every prime p, on coefficient-three M*(F_p), Γ(p)·(1,1,1)=V(p)·(1,1,1). Hence Γ(p) is transitive iff G_p is connected. The image of the CA.4 positive integer reduction map is exactly this root orbit, so these conditions are equivalent to CA.4’s prime strong-approximation predicate.
proofSteps: Use normality of V to move every coordinate permutation in a Γ-word to the right.
Every coordinate permutation fixes the root, so it disappears on evaluation.
Use CA.4’s integer generation and equivariance to identify the reduction image.
acceptance: The bridge is about the symmetric root, not equality of every Γ-orbit with every V-orbit.

nodes.title: Eventual Markoff connectivity
nodes.statement: If p>3 and Γ(p) has an orbit with complement of cardinality <p, then Γ(p) is transitive and G_p is connected. Consequently there is P₀ such that for every prime p>P₀ the coefficient-three reduction from positive integer triples is surjective; the set of disconnected primes is finite.
proofSteps: The complement is stable under all Vieta moves, so its size is divisible by p. A multiple of p smaller than p is zero.
Apply the giant theorem with ε=1/2 and transport coefficients using CA.4 for p>3.
Use the root bridge to obtain graph connectivity and the integer lift.

nodes.title: Prime strong approximation
nodes.statement: For every prime p outside the disconnected coefficient-three set, every nonzero coefficient-three solution modulo p lifts to a positive integer Markoff triple. Both full affine integral reduction maps M(Z)→M(F_p) and X(Z)→X(F_p) are surjective: add the origin, and use the factor-three equivalence for p≠3. At p=3 the coefficient-three cube is lifted by the positive root orbit, whereas coefficient-one X(F₃) consists only of the origin.

Lift the origin by the origin; transport through the twist only when legal.
Separate p=3 rather than invert 3.

nodes.title: Subgroup intersections on Markoff conics
nodes.statement: Let p>3, λ∈F_{p²}ˣ have order t>2 with a=λ+λ⁻¹∈F_p and a≠0,±2. Parametrize a nondegenerate rotation cycle by αλ^n+βλ^{-n}, with αβ=a²/(a²−4). For d∣p−1 or d∣p+1, the number of n modulo t whose second coordinate is a nonparabolic trace of order dividing d is at most (3/2) max((32td)^(1/3),16td/p). The smaller constants (6,4) quoted in the read EFLMT author copy are a separate unresolved proof obligation G4.
proofSteps: Apply CZ13 Corollary 2 to αx+β/x=y+y⁻¹, a curve of bidegree (2,2), genus 1 and four punctures, with χ=4.

For the normalized cubic let A=[1:0:0], B=[0:1:0], C=[0:0:1], D=[1:α:0]. The coordinate divisors are div(x)=B+C−A−D and div(y)=A+C−B−D, so both degrees are 2 and they are multiplicatively independent. At a torus singular point Euler’s identity would force x=βy and then αβ=1, excluded; direct gradients are nonzero at A,B,C,D. Thus the smooth plane cubic has genus 1 and χ=4.
Its coordinate functions have degrees 2 and 2; the t,d power functions have degrees 2t and 2d. Their divisors show multiplicative independence. The separating hypotheses hold because p∤td.
The bound for pairs is 3 max((32td)^(1/3),16td/p). Excluding y=±1 gives two distinct y-values per trace, so divide by 2.
Handle a=0 directly and omit parabolic coordinates only after proving they enter the cage.

nodes.title: The signed complement
nodes.statement: For p>3 in the explicit cage range, let C be the Γ-orbit containing the cage, and assume C is invariant under double sign changes. Then 4p divides # (X*(F_p)∖C). proofSteps: Double sign changes normalize the action and preserve X*. Their action is free: a fixed nonidentity sign change would force two coordinates to vanish.
Cage points of maximal order and their double-sign translates lie in the same cage orbit; propagate using normalization to get sign stability of C.
The complement is a disjoint union of four-element sign orbits and a Vieta-stable set; combine divisibility by 4 and p.

nodes.title: Effective order obstruction
nodes.statement: Suppose p>3 is in a range where the explicit cage and endgame estimates hold. If Γ is not transitive, there is d∣p−1 or d∣p+1 with either 2√(2p)/M_d(p)<d≤108M_d(p)^3, or p/(24M_d(p))≤d≤K_p^±, where K_p^±=8√p(p±1)τ(p±1)/φ(p±1), with the sign matching d. If the sharper local estimate requested in G4 is proved, the original source constants 81/4 and 6 replace 108 and 24. Both versions keep their boundary inequalities explicit.

Cover its lower coordinate orders by maximal divisors and sum the local intersection estimate: d≤(3/2)M max((32d²)^(1/3),16d²/p).
The two terms give d≤108M³ or d≥p/(24M). Count all low-order points and compare with 4p to obtain the lower bound in the first case.
Use the explicit endgame cutoff K_p^± for the upper bound in the second. Recheck equality cases instead of importing the source’s strict inequalities unchanged.

nodes.title: Reducing functions
nodes.statement: For positive m,n, a reducing map f:D(n)→D(m) satisfies f(d)≤d; (m/f(d))/(n/d)≤min(1,λ(m/f(d))/λ(n/d)); and f(d)/f(e)∈2^Z implies d/e∈2^Z. Quotients are positive rational numbers, D uses positive divisors, λ(1)=1 and λ(k) is the least prime factor for k≥2. Reducing is a predicate on maps, not an assertion that f itself is injective.
proofSteps: Express the rational inequalities over positive denominators; give the 2-power condition as equality after multiplying by nonnegative powers of 2.
Show identity maps are reducing and composition preserves all three conditions.

For coprime source and target factorizations, extend reducing maps by products. For the ratio inequality write A_i=m_i/f_i(d_i), B_i=n_i/d_i. If B_i=1 then A_i=1; discard that pair. If some A_i=1<B_i, the product ratio is at most 1/B_i≤1/λ(B₁B₂)≤λ(A₁A₂)/λ(B₁B₂). If both A_i>1, use the ordinary product/minimum identity and the factor with minimal λ(A_i). The ratio is also at most 1. This handles terminal quotients instead of replacing a ratio of minima by an unsupported inequality.

EFLMT Appendix §6, pp. 28–29 gives the sharp-cover route; BGS16 §§2–3 proves an eventual range only. All constants, removed points and nonsplit covers must survive Q2. An asymptotic O-term does not certify 3.489·10^392.

gaps.title: Sharp local constants and the quoted numerical endpoint
gaps.detail: Source finding E4: the four-punctured genus-one curve and degree-two coordinate maps give a safe (3/2)max((32td)^(1/3),16td/p) bound from CZ13, not the source’s (3/2)max((6td)^(1/3),4td/p). Either independently prove the sharper bound, or run and verify a complete certificate with the repaired constants. The published PLMS 2025 proof could not be retrieved (403); this finding concerns the dated author revision only. Source algorithms report 124720785 reduced-integer outputs in the search and 48066 outputs below the eventual cutoff (Remark 4.6, p. 26); none is a delivered certificate. The exact N and central coefficient were checked but cannot close the gap.

Propose ArithmeticDynamicsIntegralOrbits: IO.0 imports CA.4 Markoff–Hurwitz carriers/moves and adds normalized free semigroups plus the relative-character interpretation; IO.1 accelerated renewal and logarithmic-linear comparison; IO.2 integer tuple/geodesic counting and β(n); IO.3 published Cayley Chebyshev orbit and unprovided degree-count proof; IO.4 integral level-set density and the two universal cubic forms.
